implementation_notes: C ships no actor runtime, so the structure is hand-written: each actor is a struct holding private state, a mailbox (queue plus pthread_mutex_t and pthread_cond_t) and a receive loop. Messages are popped with the standard while-not-satisfied pthread_cond_wait protocol and handled one at a time; the sender transfers ownership of the heap payload and must not touch it afterwards, and shutdown is a sentinel message or a flag plus pthread_cond_broadcast. POSIX message queues (mq_open/mq_send) are the alternative when the mailbox must span processes. A pthread per actor is simple for a small number of actors, but an event loop or worker pool is needed for many actors; choose the mailbox bound and overflow policy explicitly.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait must be called in a while loop against the queue predicate; spurious wakeups and missed signals otherwise drop or duplicate messages.
The sender must transfer ownership of the message payload; retaining or freeing it after send is a use-after-free that no type system prevents.
One thread per actor does not scale to thousands of actors; multiplex actors over a small worker pool or an event loop before reaching for pthread-per-actor.
An unbounded mailbox lets a fast producer exhaust memory; bound the queue and define the full policy (block, drop, or report an error to the sender).
